exercises.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the match.
exercises.explanation: Type 1: present simple in the if-clause.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: If I had more money, I ___ a car.
exercises.explanation: Type 2: *had* in the if-clause, so *would* + base verb.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: True or false: « If she will come, I will be happy. » is correct.
exercises.explanation: False. No *will* in the if-clause: **If she comes, I will be happy.**
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with its meaning.
pairs: If I win the lottery, I will travel.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
Unless you hurry, you will be late.
same as: if you do not hurry
If I were you, I would apologise.
exercises.explanation: Type 1 for real possibility, type 2 for imaginary situations, *unless* means *if ... not*, and *If I were you* is used to give advice.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with *unless*: *If you don't revise, you will fail the test.*
exercises.model: **Unless you revise, you will fail the test.**
rubric: 1 mark: the main clause is unchanged.
exercises.explanation: *If ... not* becomes *unless* and the verb of the unless-clause is affirmative.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Write four conditional sentences: two of type 1 about next week and two of type 2 about imaginary situations.
exercises.model: If it rains on Saturday, I will read at home. If I finish my homework, I will play football. If I were a doctor, I would work in a village. If I had a magic carpet, I would visit Paris.
rubric: 1 mark each sentence: correct pattern (type 1 or type 2), correct verb forms, sensible meaning.
exercises.explanation: Type 1: present / will. Type 2: past / would.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

parts.prompt: We ___ a film two days ago.
If the bus is late, we ___ walk.
parts.explanation: Type 1: present in the if-clause, *will* in the main clause.

parts.prompt: If I ___ you, I would study more.
parts.explanation: Type 2: *If I were you, I would ...*

parts.prompt: Which sentence means « If you don't hurry, you will be late »?
choices: Unless you hurry, you will be late.
Unless you don't hurry, you will be late.
If you hurry, you will be late.
Unless you hurried, you would be late.

exercises.explanation: Find the time marker or the if-clause, then choose the tense.
